 9                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Today we 

10   are joined by Rabbi Menachem Kotlarsky, from 

11   Chabad Merkos 302 in Brooklyn.  He will deliver 

12   our invocation.  

13                Rabbi.  

14                RABBI KOTLARSKY:   As we received 

15   news of yesterday's tragic train crash, I begin 

16   with a solemn prayer for healing to those 

17   injured, comfort to the families who lost loved 

18   ones.  {in Hebrew}  May we know no more pain and 

19   suffering.  

20                Almighty God, the members of this 

21   prestigious New York State Senate stand before 

22   you today representing the people of the State 

23   of New York, elected as their leaders and 

24   bestowed with the profound responsibility of 

25   continuously guiding this state towards a 


                                                                2549

 1   greater and brighter tomorrow.

 2                {In Hebrew}  Those who dedicate 

 3   themselves faithfully to those needs of the 

 4   community, may God repay them and grant them 

 5   blessing and success in all of their deeds.  

 6                Help them recognize the awesome 

 7   power endowed upon them to create positive change 

 8   in the State of New York and indeed in the entire 

 9   world, for which this great state is a catalyst, 

10   and the decisions made in this hall reverberate 

11   across the globe.  

12                Grant the members of the Senate the 

13   strength to make their decisions guided by the 

14   steady anchor of Your fundamental universal laws 

15   given at Sinai, which are recognizing the Creator 

16   of the world, respecting the sanctity of human 

17   life and of all creatures, protecting the 

18   morality of our relationships, and upholding 

19   courts of justice.

20                May You bless the State of New York 

21   with the wisdom and courage to continue to 

22   recognize the beauty in our diverse communities 

23   created from uniqueness of each individual and 

24   our collective cultures being welcomed together, 

25   just as our Lubavitch Chabad Rebbe was welcomed 


                                                                2550

 1   75 years ago.  

 2                Allow them the perspective to 

 3   highlight the power of a single good deed in 

 4   adding light to the world.  {in Hebrew}  The 

 5   world is balanced and with one good deed can 

 6   dispel a lot of darkness.

 7                May God bless this great assembly of 

 8   the State of New York, the people in New York.  

 9   May God bless America.  And we conclude with {in 

10   Hebrew} may there always be peace.

 1   its entirety.  And would you then call on

 3                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Very good.  

 4   The Secretary will read.

 5                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 6   Resolution Number 1274, by Senator Griffo, 

 7   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

 8   proclaim May 2015 as Lupus Awareness Month in the 

 9   State of New York.  

10                "WHEREAS, Each year, the Lupus 

11   Agencies of New York State designate May as Lupus 

12   Awareness Month to show support for the 105,400 

13   New Yorkers, 1.5 million Americans and 5 million 

14   people worldwide who suffer from the often 

15   debilitating effects of lupus, a chronic 

16   autoimmune disease that can cause severe damage 

17   to the tissue and organs in the body and, in some 

18   cases, death; and 

19                "WHEREAS, Each year, thousands of  

20   people are newly diagnosed with lupus, the great 

21   majority of whom are young people in the prime of 

22   their lives, and 90 percent of whom are women; 

23   and 

24                "WHEREAS, Lupus is most prevalent 

25   among African-Americans, Hispanics, Native 


                                                                2553

 1   Americans, Asians; tragically, thousands of 

 2   people die from lupus each year because a cure 

 3   remains elusive; and 

 4                "WHEREAS, Many health professionals 

 5   are unaware of symptoms and health effects of 

 6   lupus, causing people with lupus to suffer for 

 7   many years before they obtain a correct diagnosis 

 8   and medical treatment, demonstrating the need for 

 9   increased public and professional awareness of 

10   lupus; and 

11                "WHEREAS, Medical research efforts 

12   into lupus and the discovery of safer, more 

13   effective treatments for Lupus patients are 

14   underfunded in comparison with diseases of 

15   comparable magnitude and severity; and 

16                "WHEREAS, Increasing community 

17   awareness and focusing public attention on lupus 

18   and its devastating impact on patients' lives 

19   will provide hope for a better future for those 

20   affected; and 

21                "WHEREAS, The Lupus Agencies of 

22   New York State are dedicated to improving the 

23   quality of life for individuals with lupus, and 

24   their loved ones, by providing education, support 

25   and outreach services, and promoting programs of 


                                                                2554

 1   awareness, advocacy, and research; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body 

 3   recognizes the needs of those chronically ill 

 4   people who are living with lupus and urges all  

 5   citizens to support the search for a cure and 

 6   assist those individuals and families who deal 

 7   with this devastating disease on a daily  basis;  

 8   now, therefore, be it 

 9                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

10   Body pause in its deliberations to memorialize 

11   Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to proclaim May 2015 as 

12   Lupus Awareness Month in the State of New York; 

13   and be it further 

14                "RESOLVED, That copies of this 

15   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

16   the Honorable Andrew M. Cuomo, Governor of the  

17   State of New York, and the Lupus Agencies of 

18   New York State."

19                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Senator 

20   Griffo.

21                SENATOR GRIFFO:   Thank you, 

22   Mr. President.

23                As you have all heard, the 

24   resolution gives you some very telling statistics 

25   and discusses the challenges that so many face 


                                                                2555

 1   today across this country and this state.

 2                So I'm pleased today just to 

 3   acknowledge and recognize some of the fine 

 4   individuals from the Lupus Agencies of New York 

 5   State who are with us today.  

 6                Kathleen Arntsen has been a strong 

 7   advocate from my area for a long time in trying 

 8   to continue to make sure that we have proper 

 9   attention and the resources are being devoted and 

10   dedicated to the research that's necessary, as 

11   well as the fight against this autoimmune disease 

12   which has affected so many.  

13                So today I just want to stand and -- 

14   they gave me two bracelets here to wear, one for 

15   research and one for the fight -- I want to thank 

16   you all for the commitment that you have made for 

17   your dedication.  

18                And really you have the undying 

19   gratitude of so many people, so that we continue 

20   to ensure that people are made aware, informed, 

21   and that we continue to do whatever we can to 

22   devote the resources to fight this autoimmune 

23   disease, not only to call attention to it but 

24   someday to find a cure.  So I compliment and 

25   applaud all of you for your efforts and your 


                                                                2556

 1   advocacy.  

 2                And I want to recognize all of them 

 3   from all parts of the state today, from 

 4   Long Island, New York City, Central New York, the 

 5   western part of the state, the Southern Tier, and 

 6   the Capital District.  From all of New York, 

 7   thank you so much for what you all do.  

 8                If you would all please rise, and we 

 9   can acknowledge the Lupus Agencies of New York 

10   State.

11                (Applause.)

12                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Senator 

13   Savino.

14                SENATOR SAVINO:   Thank you, 

15   Mr. President.

16                I also rise, first to thank Senator 

17   Griffo for bringing this resolution again, and to 

18   thank the advocates of the Lupus Foundation, and 

19   particularly their lobbyist, Kathleen Arntsen, 

20   who comes here every year to try and raise 

21   awareness about lupus and the effects that it has 

22   on women.  

23                For the past couple of years I've 

24   carried a bill with Assemblywoman Crystal 

25   Peoples-Stokes to create an education and 


                                                                2557

 1   outreach program in the Health Department and to 

 2   create a Lupus Research Advisory Council.  

 3                Senator Parker, who's not in the 

 4   chamber at the moment, also has a bill that would 

 5   create a taxpayer check-off box on income tax 

 6   returns to help provide funding for a Lupus 

 7   Education and Prevention Fund.

 8                This is a devastating disease that 

 9   affects women, and particularly African-American 

10   women.  

11                In 2011 the FDA approved, for the 

12   first time in 50 years, the first new drug to 

13   deal with lupus and the terrible disease of 

14   lupus.  It's a drug called Benlysta.  It has had 

15   some effect, a positive effect on some women, but 

16   not enough yet.  We're not seeing all of the 

17   potential benefits of it.  But the sad reality is 

18   that for the 50 years prior to that, there 

19   were -- really only corticosteroids and aspirin 

20   was the approved treatment for lupus.  

21                And just to keep this in mind, lupus 

22   strikes women 10 to 15 times more frequently than 

23   men.  That's why we call it really a woman's 

24   disease.  Ninety percent of the individuals who 

25   have been diagnosed with lupus are women of 


                                                                2558

 1   childbearing age.  African-American women are 

 2   three times more likely to get lupus than 

 3   Caucasian women.  

 4                Most of those women, though, have 

 5   been through multiple doctors and multiple 

 6   misdiagnoses before they finally figure out what 

 7   it is that's affecting them.  And in the meantime 

 8   their health suffers in a terrible way, it 

 9   affects their home, their family life, it affects 

10   their employment life, it affects every aspect of 

11   their life.  

12                So I'm happy to stand with Senator 

13   Griffo again as we take up this resolution, and I 

14   hope that we will be able to make the argument 

15   next year, hopefully in the budget, that the 

16   State Department of Health needs to do more, they 

17   need to put forward a research and education 

18   program to alert women to the very dangers, so 

19   that those women who are suffering silently and 

20   not knowing what's wrong with them will know to 

21   ask their doctor to test them for lupus.  That's 

22   what this should be about.  

23                And I want to thank Senator Griffo 

24   and the advocates for sharing their stories and 

25   their pain and suffering to make positive change 


                                                                2559

 1   for women now and in the future.  

 2                Thank you, Mr. President.

 1   voluntary basis, for restaurants in an outdoor

10   that we were meeting with the folks who think 

11   this is a good thing, that they can take a step 

12   forward to have a person's best friend with them 

13   when they dine.  And I thank you very much.
